spec_family.name: New Construction Interior Trim Stain/Clear Coat
spec_family.description: Covers stain application, sanding sealer, and clear topcoat for 7 interior trim types in new construction. Combined spec with coating_type dimension (stain_clear, stain_only, clear_only). Stain phase includes wipe step for all methods. Sealer and clear phases use independent application method selection. Uses LF as primary UOM (1 LF = 1 SF per PCA standard for trim <1 ft width). Material systems are product-role-based recommendations — contractor retains discretion on product selection. Context prefix TRST avoids collision with paint counterpart SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT (prefix TRIM).

includes: Stain application on bare wood trim (brush+wipe, roll+wipe, spray+wipe)
Second stain coat application (optional, user-selectable)
Sanding sealer application (0-2 coats, QT-driven defaults)
Clear topcoat application (1-3 coats, QT-driven defaults)
Bare wood preparation (inspect, sand 120-150 grit, fill defects with wood filler, grain raise for waterborne, tack clean)
Wood conditioner application (softwood + stain, unless gel stain)
Interstage sanding between sealer coats (220-320 grit)
Interstage sanding between clear coats (320-400 grit)
Stain dry verification before sealer/clear application
Floor perimeter protection (drop cloths)
Wall masking at trim-to-wall edge (spray or when walls are SS_PAINTED_*)
Fixture covers near spray zone
Final inspection and touch-up
Baseboard stain/clear coat
Crown molding stain/clear coat
Chair rail stain/clear coat
Wainscot cap/rail stain/clear coat
Shadow box / picture frame molding stain/clear coat
Panel molding stain/clear coat
Picture rail stain/clear coat

excludes.item: Interior repaint stain (stripping existing finish, recoating)

excludes.route_to: SF_TRIM_EXT_RP or future exterior trim NC stain spec

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary configuration dimension — drives layer stack, material systems, and module activation. stain_clear is the full stain + sealer + clear workflow. stain_only applies stain without topcoat. clear_only applies clear without stain (natural wood or pre-stained).
configuration_dimensions.notes: stain_clear is the professional standard for interior trim. stain_only is rare (unprotected stain). clear_only for natural wood look or pre-stained surfaces.

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline, and coat count defaults. Does NOT affect application quality (binary at all tiers).
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3=budget (1 stain + 0 sealer + 1 clear = 2 coats). QT4=standard (1 stain + 1 sealer + 2 clear = 4 coats). QT5=premium (1 stain + 2 sealer + 3 clear = 6 coats). All coat counts user-overridable.

configuration_dimensions.description: Stain application technique. All stain methods include a wipe step to control color depth.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Brush is default — most control over color uniformity. Roll is fastest for large flat areas. Spray is for production volume. All methods include wipe-back step.

configuration_dimensions.description: Clear coat application technique. No roll option — causes air bubbles in clear coat.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Brush is default for control. Spray for production volume. Roll PROHIBITED for clear coat (air bubble defects). Lacquer clear requires spray.

configuration_dimensions.description: Clear coat sheen. Drives product selection. Not applicable for stain_only.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Satin is most popular for residential trim. No sheen/QT gate — all sheens available at all tiers (unlike paint specs).

configuration_dimensions.description: Number of stain coats. User-selectable with default of 1.
configuration_dimensions.notes: 1 coat is standard. 2 coats for deeper color saturation. Default 1 at all QT levels.

configuration_dimensions.description: Number of sanding sealer coats. User-selectable with QT-driven defaults.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3 skips sealer (budget). QT4 uses 1 coat. QT5 uses 2 coats for maximum film build. All user-overridable.

configuration_dimensions.description: Number of clear topcoats. User-selectable with QT-driven defaults.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3 uses 1 coat (budget). QT4 uses 2 coats (standard). QT5 uses 3 coats (maximum protection and depth).

configuration_dimensions.description: Trim profile complexity. Controls production rate modifiers.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 7.2. Simple=flat/square edge. Standard=ogee/cove. Complex=multi-piece/built-up. Ornate=dentil/egg-and-dart. Applied per trim item.

configuration_dimensions.description: Wood species grouping. Drives wood conditioner activation for softwood.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Softwood (pine, poplar, alder) requires pre-stain wood conditioner to prevent blotchy absorption — unless gel stain is selected (gel stain controls blotch inherently). Hardwood (oak, maple, cherry, walnut) does not need conditioner.

paintable_items.name: Baseboard
paintable_items.counting_rules: Total linear footage of baseboard. 1 LF = 1 SF per PCA standard for trim <1 ft width.
paintable_items.notes: Most common trim type. Present in nearly all rooms.

paintable_items.name: Crown molding
paintable_items.counting_rules: Total linear footage of crown molding at wall-ceiling junction.
paintable_items.notes: Height modifier typically applies — crown is at ceiling height. May need step/extension ladder.

paintable_items.name: Chair rail
paintable_items.counting_rules: Total linear footage of chair rail at wall mid-height.
paintable_items.notes: Standard height (~32-36 inches from floor). No height modifier.

paintable_items.name: Wainscot cap/rail
paintable_items.counting_rules: Total linear footage of wainscot cap rail.
paintable_items.notes: Often paired with chair rail. No height modifier.

paintable_items.name: Shadow box / picture frame molding
paintable_items.counting_rules: Total linear footage of shadow box or picture frame molding on walls.
paintable_items.notes: Decorative wall molding. Profile complexity often 'complex' or 'ornate'.

paintable_items.name: Panel molding
paintable_items.counting_rules: Total linear footage of panel molding.
paintable_items.notes: Applied wall panel molding. May be simple or complex profile.

paintable_items.name: Picture rail
paintable_items.counting_rules: Total linear footage of picture rail near ceiling.
paintable_items.notes: Near ceiling height — height modifier may apply. Less common in NC.

variants.notes: Budget stain+clear. 1 stain + 1 clear = 2 total coats. No sealer. Fastest clear workflow.
Standard stain+clear. 1 stain + 1 sealer + 2 clear = 4 total coats. Professional residential standard.
Premium stain+clear. 1 stain + 2 sealer + 3 clear = 6 total coats. Maximum film build and depth.
Production variant. Roll stain (speed) + spray clear (finish quality). Common NC production workflow.
Stain-only, no clear coat. Minimal workflow — stain + wipe only. Unprotected finish.
Clear-only on natural or pre-stained wood. 1 sealer + 2 clear = 3 coats. No stain application.
Premium clear-only spray. 2 sealer + 3 clear = 5 coats. Lacquer-compatible variant.
Premium all-spray. Maximum production speed at highest quality tier. Full protection required.

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: application_method_stain = spray OR application_method_clear = spray, or any method when walls are SS_PAINTED_*
required_paintscope_inputs.description: Wall masking LF at trim-to-wall edge
Count of fixtures (outlets/switches) near spray zone requiring covers

protection_zones_required.notes: Runner-style drop cloths along trim perimeter for drip catching. Stain is especially prone to dripping. Excluded when floor is subfloor.
Tape + paper masking at trim-to-wall edge for spray method. Also required for any method when walls are SS_PAINTED_*.
Cover outlets/switches near spray zone. Spray only.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Stained trim adjacent to painted walls. Stain and wall are always different finishes. Protection only (masking for spray or when walls SS_PAINTED_*).
Door casing and door frame often share stain/clear finish. May be stained in same session.
Crown molding touches finished ceiling. Spray method may require light masking at crown-ceiling junction.

valid_input_states.notes: Bare wood is the primary input state for stain specs. clear_only also accepts SS_STAINED (pre-stained wood needing topcoat only). SS_CLEAR_COATED as input is RP scope (not this spec).

output_state.notes: stain_clear and clear_only produce SS_CLEAR_COATED. stain_only produces SS_STAINED (unprotected).

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: When walls are finished (SS_PAINTED_*), wall masking at trim-to-wall edge required for ALL methods. Stain is harder to clean off painted walls than paint is.
When walls are unfinished (typical NC), spray method still requires masking at trim-to-wall edge.
When walls are unfinished and non-spray method, no wall protection needed. Typical NC scenario.

site_condition_rules.effect: Floor protection excluded when floor is subfloor.
site_condition_rules.notes: NC often has subfloor during trim staining. Finished/partial floors require drop cloth runners.

site_condition_rules.effect: Height modifier applies for elevated trim (crown molding, picture rail). H2=1.30 for 9-12ft, H3=1.50 for 13ft+.
site_condition_rules.notes: Per Modifier_Registry. Standard baseboard at floor level has no height modifier.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Stain trim typically occurs BEFORE wall finishing in NC sequence. Staining requires bare wood — cannot stain over primed or painted trim.
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Setup → Prep (sand, fill, grain raise, condition) → Stain coat 1 (+wipe) → [Stain coat 2] → Stain dry → Sealer coat 1 → [Sealer interstage → Sealer coat 2] → Sealer sand → Clear coat 1 → [Clear interstage → Clear coat 2] → [Clear coat 3] → Final inspect → Cleanup
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Setup floor protection → Wall masking (if applicable) → Fixture covers (spray only) → Apply coats → Teardown
sequencing_notes.dry_times: Stain: 4-8 hrs (oil), 2 hrs (waterborne) before sealer/clear. Sealer: 2-4 hrs between coats. Clear: 4-6 hrs between coats (oil poly), 2 hrs (WB poly).
sequencing_notes.notes: Unlike paint specs, stain has no companion prime spec — bare wood prep and all coating layers in one spec.

relationships.notes: Stain counterpart to SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT. Establishes canonical stain/clear module architecture for all 10 interior stain specs.

sections_used: Surfaces <1 ft width measured as 1 LF

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for NC interior trim stain/clear coat (Tier 1 in interior stain spec rollout). Key features: coating_type dimension (stain_clear/stain_only/clear_only), 7 trim types (door/window casing excluded — routed to their own stain specs), independent stain and clear application methods, user-selectable coat counts with QT-driven defaults (QT3: 2 total, QT4: 4 total, QT5: 6 total), 4 stain + 2 sealer + 3 clear material systems as recommendations, profile complexity modifiers (0.85-1.40), wood_species_group for conditioner activation, SS_BARE input with SS_STAINED/SS_CLEAR_COATED outputs per coating_type, up to 14 SOP modules, context prefix TRST.
